page: Microsoft Azure F4alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with a high base clock speed of 4.5 GHz, this server allocates one physical core per vCPU. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor features a 32 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration.

This instance includes 472 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, allowing for high-speed disk configurations. Virtualization is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system lacks dedicated GPU accelerators, relying entirely on the AMD EPYC processor for computational workloads.

In benchmark testing, the F4alds_v7 demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance, scoring 3678.58 in stress-ng single-core tests and achieving high throughput in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth fall into the average tier, with a passmark CPU score of 12917.96 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 14901.33. For language model tasks, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 343.49 tokens per second on small 135M models, but drops to a weak 30.42 tokens per second for prompt processing on medium 7B models, highlighting a performance tradeoff when handling larger model architectures.

Given its low memory-to-CPU ratio, the F4alds_v7 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-bound workloads that do not demand large memory footprints. It is suited for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight web serving, and small-scale database operations, where the high 4.5 GHz clock speed can be leveraged without incurring the costs of excess RAM.
